transcript:
Header: 2026-03-03 15:00 PT | Duration: ~62m
Attendees: Jamie Carter (Redwood AE), Ravi Singh (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood Solutions); Maria Lopez (Novum Head ML Infra), Ethan Park (CTO), Samir Patel (Security), Olivia Chen (ML Eng)

Auto-summary (auto): Deep technical dive on long-context (128k+) runtime behavior; discussed KV cache strategies, chunking/segmentation, attention optimizations, quantization trade-offs, and on-prem/VPC requirements. Agreed next steps: share benchmarks, run Dedicated 48h test, schedule pilot.

Topics: 1) Long-context memory strategies (KV cache, chunking) 2) Throughput & latency tradeoffs for 128k 3) Quantization and perf/accuracy tradeoffs 4) VPC/on-prem integration and security controls 5) Benchmark plan and pilot scope

00:00 Jamie: Hey everyone thanks for carving out time. quick intro from our side, i'm jamie carter, AE, and ravi's gonna run the deep dive.
00:14 Maria: Thanks. i'll kick off with our goals — we want to index multi-hour clinical notes, roughly 120k-200k token sessions, low tail latency, and strict audit. curious on redwood's long context story.
00:30 Ravi: Great. high-level — our runtime supports segmented attention and a streaming chunk model; for 128k we typically do a hybrid: KV caching for hot prefixes + chunked attention windows to bound compute.
00:47 Ethan: When you say chunked attention, do you mean sliding window or hierarchical?
00:52 Ravi: both options. for clinical docs we prefer hierarchical + sparse inter-chunk cross-attn. practically we window at ~8k-16k tokens, keep KV cache for earlier chunks, and run cross-chunk passes where needed.
01:10 Olivia: does that add a lot of latency on cross-chunk ops?
01:15 Ravi: there's a latency step — cross-chunk passes are heavier, but we schedule them async for lower-priority requests. for sync serving we do on-demand cross passes with configurable SLOs.
01:28 Samir: security question — can KV cache be encrypted customer-side (KMS/HSM)? we need no cleartext persisted in your control plane.
01:36 Jamie: yes you can host the KV cache in your VPC for Private mode; we also support envelope encryption with customer KMS. we'll share the KMS integration doc.
01:50 Maria: nice. can you quantify throughput? tokens/sec for a 128k session on dedicated GPU pool?
01:56 Ravi: rough numbers — on an A100-equivalent Dedicated pod with batching tuned, you can get sustained ~2.5-4k input tokens/sec for generation workloads at 128k windows, but it depends heavily on chunking, quantization and model architecture. with 8-bit quant and kernel tuning we saw up to 6k tokens/sec in synthetic tests.
02:20 Ethan: that's pretty wide. what's the latency tail like?
02:24 Ravi: p50 might be fine but p95/p99 depends: cross-chunk passes push p99 higher. for interactive SLOs we recommend mixing prefix-KV caching to reduce work on hot prefixes and use streaming to surface early tokens while backfilling longer cross passes.
02:40 Olivia: transcription note — we tried K V cash in our PoC and it got messy — any gotchas?
02:46 Ravi: ha, yes 'K V cash' — common transcript artifact. practical gotchas: cache invalidation on model rollouts, consistency across replica pools, and memory growth on long-lived sessions. our runtime has eviction policies and TTLs, and we expose metrics for KV size per session.
03:05 Maria: talk about quantization — we care about accuracy for clinical reasoning. what quant profiles do you recommend for 128k?
03:13 Ravi: for accuracy-sensitive tasks we avoid aggressive 4-bit quant for final answer-generation; we use mixed quant: 8-bit for attention/projection layers + selective higher-precision for MLPs, or we keep the final pass at 16-bit. this gives ~1.5-2x perf improvement without large quality regression in our evals. we'll share the quant profile matrix.
03:36 Ethan: any kernel-level optimizations specific to long context?
03:40 Ravi: yes, we implement causal attention tiling and KV cache re-use with fused attention kernels. for very long sequences we use block-sparse attention on chunk boundaries and optimize for memory-bound cases; the runtime picks kernels by model signature and seq-length distribution.
03:59 Jamie: quick note — we have an internal benchmark deck, link: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/128k (will share externally as deck v2)
04:12 Maria: for on-prem, how much infra do we need? gpu count? network?
04:18 Ravi: depends on SLA. for a 1k rps equivalent of 128k sessions you need large-scale pooling—most customers start with Dedicated pools sized per expected concurrency. for on-prem private installs, we recommend a minimum of 8xA100 or equivalent with NVLink fabric for high-throughput KV sync, and provisioning for ~1.2-1.5x memory overhead for KV caches.
04:45 Samir: and RBAC / audit? we need per-token level logging?
04:50 Jamie: we provide per-request trace IDs, detailed token-level cost breakdowns in the console, and audit logs that can be pushed to your SIEM. on Private you can keep logs in your S3 and we can forward.
05:02 Olivia: i want to dig into chunking strategy — our data is hierarchical: note -> sections -> paragraphs. is there a recommended segmentation?
05:11 Ravi: yes map your chunk boundaries to semantics — prefer boundary alignment to avoid cross-chunk attention for tightly coupled text. use overlap windows (e.g., 128-512 tokens) to maintain context. combine with a document index so you only load necessary chunks for a query.
05:30 Maria: can you share sample configs?
05:34 Ravi: yeah we'll include sample chunking configs and a script to simulate token distributions.
05:40 Ethan: okay cost question — dedicated vs hosted. if we go Hosted and hit 200k sessions / day, how do we control costs?
05:49 Jamie: we surface cost drivers: tokens generated, KV cache memory retention, and cross-pass compute. Optimize by using prefix caches, lower-precision where acceptable, and batching similar requests. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching/quant profiles per workload.
06:05 Maria: curious about failure modes — if a node fails while KV cache is local, do you lose the session?
06:12 Ravi: we have three options: 1) best-effort fallbacks to a cold-start model (slower), 2) replicated KV stores for Dedicated/Private with async replication, or 3) persistent KV in customer-managed storage (VPC) — tradeoff is latency vs durability.
06:31 Samir: for replication across AZs, what's bandwidth cost?
06:36 Ravi: depends on KV churn; for long-context doc ingestion typical steady-state replication is moderate, spikes on heavy writes. we'll share a calculator.
06:45 Maria: do you support streaming partial results while backgrounding cross-chunk scoring?
06:50 Ravi: yes that's our recommended pattern: stream early tokens and run non-blocking cross-chunk refinement; deliver final coherent result when ready. UI-level stitching is recommended so product can show partial then final.
07:05 Olivia: any example production customers doing 128k+?
07:09 Jamie: we have a few—financial/health customers on Private and Dedicated; names we can't disclose in detail but we can share anonymized perf curves.
07:18 Ethan: about quant: are you using GPTQ-like approaches or proprietary kernels?
07:22 Ravi: mixture. we support GPTQ-style quant for model weight compression and have optimized kernels for 8/4-bit runtimes. newer 4-bit kernels are still experimental for critical accuracy workloads.
07:36 Jamie: side note — policy: when customers want full on-prem air-gapped, we ship a Private build and provide ops runbook.
07:44 Samir: does private build require any contacting home? must be zero outbound.
07:48 Jamie: we support fully air-gapped installs; optional telemetry can be disabled. we still need a license key exchange process you can do via offline bundle.
07:58 Maria: let's talk benchmarks. what artifacts will you give?
08:02 Ravi: we'll provide: 1) raw throughput logs 2) per-token latency histograms (p50/p95/p99) 3) KV cache hit/miss rates 4) memory/CPU/GPU utilization 5) quant-profile accuracy deltas against our eval set.
08:20 Olivia: perfect. and what about rolling model updates without invalidating caches?
08:25 Ravi: we version the KV schema; small patch rollouts can reuse caches with a compatibility shim; larger architecture changes require reindexing. we'll show a migration plan in the docs.
08:42 Ethan: are there any open-source tools you recommend for simulating 128k live traffic?
08:46 Ravi: we use a harness we can share (script + docker): simulates token distributions, chunk overlap, hot prefixes, and replay. we'll push to the sandbox repo.
08:58 Maria: outstanding security items: SOC2 report, encryption-at-rest details, KMS/HSM support, RBAC, retention windows.
09:07 Jamie: noted — we'll send the security pack; also include our SOC2 type II and a checklist for on-prem compliance.
09:15 Samir: last question: how do you handle prompt injection across long-context? if someone appends malicious instructions in later chunks?
09:24 Ravi: two defenses: 1) policy filters applied per-chunk plus aggregated scoring; 2) prompt engineering patterns that privilege earlier trusted prefixes (e.g., system prompt anchoring) and treat later chunks as lower-priority. we also expose chunk-level provenance so you can audit and redact.
09:46 Maria: ok this is helpful. any cost estimate for initial pilot (3 months) with Dedicated + 8xA100-ish footprint?
09:54 Jamie: rough ballpark — we'll send a pricing worksheet; typically initial committed reduces unit cost significantly vs pay-as-you-go. will include both Dedicated and private licensing options.
10:06 Olivia: can we get an example config for overlap sizes and eviction TTLs?
10:11 Ravi: yes, sample config in the repo. recommended: overlap 256 tokens, eviction TTL 24-72 hours depending on workload and privacy.
10:22 Ethan: schedule — we'd like a pilot starting mid-march; need internal signoffs from security and infra.
10:27 Jamie: perfect. next steps recap in a sec.

10:30 Recap / Next steps:
10:31 Jamie: 1) we'll share the benchmark deck + raw logs (Jamie) 2) Ravi to provide harness + run 48h Dedicated run with your sample dataset 3) Security pack to Samir 4) schedule pilot kickoff week of 2026-03-15.
10:48 Maria: thanks. can you also share sample SLA templates?
10:52 Jamie: yes, included in the pack.
11:00 Meeting end.
